the_critical_correction.what_round_159_claimed: OpenFOAM v1912 installed via apt; icoFoam works; partial infrastructure success
the_critical_correction.what_round_159_got_wrong: Round 159 treated icoFoam success as evidence that the clotFoam world is available. This is an epistemic error. icoFoam is a GENERIC CFD solver; clotFoam is a SPECIALIZED solver with platelet-mediated coagulation physics. Running icoFoam does NOT validate clotFoam.

the_version_mismatch.are_these_the_same: NO — OpenFOAM v9 (Foundation) and OpenFOAM v1912 (ESI) are DIFFERENT distributions with different source code, different APIs, and different library ABIs. They share a common ancestry but diverged in 2014. Code written for v9 may not compile against v1912, and vice versa.
the_version_mismatch.evidence: clotFoam README explicitly states: 'clotFoam has been developed with the OpenFoam v9 libraries.' The apt package provides v1912, not v9.

the_epistemic_distinction.icoFoam_validation_equals: fluid solver control — confirms that a generic CFD solver can run on this system
the_epistemic_distinction.icoFoam_validation_does_NOT_equal: clotFoam validation — does NOT confirm that the specific platelet/coagulation physics solver works
the_epistemic_distinction.openfoam_1912_working_does_NOT_equal: OpenFOAM v9 working — different versions, different ABIs

the_fidelity_lesson.general_principle: A solver executing successfully does NOT mean the required external world is available. The version, distribution, and physics fidelity must ALL match the scientific target.
the_fidelity_lesson.application_to_C5: icoFoam (v1912) running ≠ clotFoam (v9) validated. The system must distinguish 'generic CFD solver works' from 'specific clotFoam physics solver works'.
